To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean field approximation for a scalar field in a time dependent expanding background can be cast in the form of a time independent functional Schrodinger evolution equation, that the mean field solution of the time independent equation is self similar and that the self similarity is a consequence of the constraint on the expansion rate.

the mean-field approximation to the time-dependent Schrodinger functional equation for a scalar field in a Robertson-Walker background, with a time-dependent scale transformation of the field argument, has a time-dependent Hamiltonian which includes a time-odd constraint term.

1) the mean field equation for a self similar solution of the evolution equation for a scalar field in a Friedmann-Lemaître universe with a self interaction term is a functional Schrodigner equation whose hamilton operator is a function of the scale transformation parameter and the time derivative of the field; and 2) the self-similar solution of this mean field equation is a Gaussian wave packet whose center follows the classical evolution equation for a free particle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: what is the effect of an expanding universe on the quantum evolution of a scalar field? We find a self consistent solution of the evolution equation which is self similar in time.
the evolution of a quantum scalar field in a Robertson-Walker geometry with a self-interaction term in the Lagrangian.
the study of the quantum field in the presence of a gravitational field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self similar solutions of the mean field approximation are a general feature of the evolution equation, which is a consequence of the time-odd term.
the mean field approximation of the functional Schrodenger equation of a scalar self interacting field in an expanding space-time is exactly solvable.
the self-similar solutions of the evolution of a scalar field with self-interaction in the expanding geometry are not the most general solutions of the evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the solutions of the mean field equations for the interacting case can be obtained by the solutions of the free field case, provided the latter are multiplied by a factor which is a function of the time and the scale parameter.

the solutions of the functional Schrodigner equation for interacting fields in an expanding background, are the same as the solutions of the same functional Schrodinger equations with a time-odd constraint on the current.
, in the mean field approximation, a self similar expansion of a scalar field is possible only if the field is massless or if the expansion rate is exactly proportional to the mass of the field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mean field approximation of the evolution equation is a self similar equation which can be solved by the method of separation of variables.
the mean field approximation for interacting fields is not self similar and that this feature is related to the fact that the hamiltonian is not time independent.
the mean field equation is equivalent to a time-independent equation for an effective potential.
